channel.title: Crypto Readout
channel.description: Crypto Readout reports on Bitcoin, Ethereum and altcoin markets, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, network upgrades and crypto regulation worldwide.

item.title: What Minimum Received Means on a Crypto Swap
item.description: Minimum received sets the lowest output a swap will accept; see how the quote, slippage tolerance and router check work, and when a trade will revert.

item.title: How to Budget Price Impact for TRON Treasury Swaps
item.description: Budget a TRON treasury swap by comparing its quote with pool depth, setting a loss limit, and checking how route, fees and execution change net proceeds.

item.title: A TRON treasury buys TRX, then stakes it to vote
item.description: TRON has no separate voting token: a treasury buys TRX, stakes it for TRON Power, casts votes for Super Representatives and plans around lockup and custody.

item.title: How Treasury Teams Reconcile XMR Bridge Transfers
item.description: XMR bridge reconciliation joins private Monero deposits to destination-chain releases through wallet records, transfer references and explicit exception handling.

item.title: The State Machine Behind a Monero Bridge Deposit
item.description: A Monero deposit monitor must reconcile wallet scans, chain inclusion and confirmation policy before it triggers the bridge’s next step or marks funds available.

item.title: How zerofi turns Monero into zXMR on Sepolia
item.description: The XMR-to-zXMR route sends Monero to a bridge address, waits for confirmations, then mints a Sepolia token, so users should account for testnet and bridge risks.

item.title: Choose a USDC Route by Checking the Destination First
item.description: Choose a USDC route by matching the destination chain, accepted token, and fee budget; the same ticker can represent assets that move differently.

item.title: Pay a Polygon Invoice by Matching the Network, Token and Address
item.description: Pay a Polygon invoice by matching its network, token contract, amount and recipient, then send the stablecoin from a funded wallet and check confirmation.

item.title: Why a Polygon PoS Withdrawal Can Stay Pending
item.description: A Polygon PoS withdrawal burns tokens first, then waits for a checkpoint on Ethereum before you can submit the proof and claim the locked tokens.

item.title: Four Checks That Make Cross-Chain Retries Idempotent
item.description: A safe cross-chain retry preserves one message identity, records destination execution atomically and handles partial workflows without minting or spending twice.

item.title: When Is a Cross-Chain Transfer Actually Complete?
item.description: A cross-chain transfer is complete only after the destination chain records the delivery; a source-chain confirmation shows the request began, not that the asset arrived.

item.title: How Omnichain Apps Coordinate State Across Chains
item.description: Omnichain apps use messages to coordinate state, token supply and liquidity across networks; define authority and recovery before adding chains.

item.title: How Stablecoins Fund Payouts Across Networks
item.description: Stablecoin payouts across chains depend on the route, the asset received and confirmation rules; map each step before sending funds to a recipient on another network.

item.title: How Exchange Liquidity Shapes Cross-Chain Routes
item.description: Exchange-liquidity routes trade through a centralized venue before withdrawal; compare them with pool and solver routes by settlement, cost, custody and delivery risk.

item.title: How Bridged Crypto Reaches Your Wallet
item.description: A bridged token reaches your wallet only when the source chain, route, destination network and recipient address line up; learn how to check each step.

item.title: Why BSC Token Decimals Change the Balance You See
item.description: A BEP-20 balance is stored as an integer and displayed using the token’s decimals setting, so the same raw amount can look larger or smaller in a wallet.

item.title: Why Transfer Taxes Change a Token Swap Quote
item.description: Transfer taxes can make an AMM quote differ from what reaches a wallet; the gap depends on where the token charges and how the router measures output.

item.title: What Bridge Address Compatibility Checks Before a Transfer
item.description: Bridge address compatibility means matching the destination chain, address format and receiving account rules so a cross-chain transfer reaches an account that can use it.

item.title: How an Ethereum deposit becomes a valid bridge message
item.description: An Ethereum bridge deposit is authenticated through a confirmed contract event, a cross-chain message and a Mantle-side check before tokens are credited.

item.title: Mantle Bridge routes: choosing a transfer path
item.description: Mantle Bridge routes depend on direction, asset and destination. Learn how the official Ethereum–Mantle transfer works and what to check before signing.
